concept_tested: Recall of the definition of excretion as distinct from secretion and egestion
stem: Which one of the following statements defines excretion?

options.A: Release of a useful product formed by a gland into a duct or into the blood
options.B: Removal of unabsorbed and undigested substances from the alimentary canal
options.C: Elimination of metabolic waste products from the body
options.D: Breaking down of complex substances into simpler ones inside the cells

correct_answer_text: Elimination of metabolic waste products from the body

distractor_rationale.A: This describes secretion, in which the substance released is put to use by the body; the student treats every outward movement of a substance as excretion.
distractor_rationale.B: This describes digestive waste, which is made of substances that have never entered the body cells, so it is not a metabolic waste product.
distractor_rationale.D: This describes the catabolic side of metabolism, which produces the wastes; it is not their elimination.

solution: Excretion is the elimination of metabolic waste products from the body. The wastes concerned are formed inside body cells, which separates excretion from the removal of digestive wastes and from the release of useful secretions.
formula_principle: Excretion is defined as the elimination of metabolic waste products, that is, of by-products formed inside the body cells.
common_misconception: Students widen excretion to cover any substance leaving the body, including undigested food and glandular secretions.

options.B: It makes their blood hypertonic to the surrounding sea water and so drives excess salts out through the gills
options.C: It makes their blood isotonic to fresh water and so prevents the entry of salts from the sea
options.D: It makes their blood isotonic to the surrounding sea water and so prevents the loss of water by exosmosis

correct_answer_text: It makes their blood isotonic to the surrounding sea water and so prevents the loss of water by exosmosis

distractor_rationale.A: A body fluid more dilute than sea water would lose water to the surroundings, which is the very outcome the retained urea prevents.
distractor_rationale.B: The retained urea is described as matching the blood to sea water, not as exceeding it, and salt removal is not the stated purpose.
distractor_rationale.C: Sharks are marine, so the reference fluid is sea water; matching the blood to fresh water would not solve their osmotic problem.

solution: By retaining urea, sharks keep their body fluid isotonic to the surrounding marine water. Since there is then no osmotic difference across the body surface, water is not lost by exosmosis.
formula_principle: Osmoregulation by solute retention: sharks retain urea in the blood so that the body fluid becomes isotonic to sea water, which prevents water loss by exosmosis.
common_misconception: Students assume that all wastes must be removed as completely as possible and miss the osmotic use a retained waste can serve.

concept_tested: Ranking animals by the water cost of their nitrogenous waste through their mode of excretion
stem: Four animals are given: a land snail, a shark, a bony fish and a camel. Use the quoted figures of about 300 to 500 ml of water per gram for ammonia, about 50 ml per gram for urea and about 5 to 10 ml per gram for uric acid. Which of these animals eliminates 1 gm of its nitrogenous waste with the smallest quantity of water?

options.A: The land snail
options.B: The shark
options.C: The bony fish
options.D: The camel

correct_answer_text: The land snail

distractor_rationale.B: The shark is ureotelic, so about 50 ml of water per gram is needed; it is economical compared with an ammonotelic animal but not the most economical here.
distractor_rationale.C: Bony fishes are ammonotelic, and ammonia is the costliest waste in water terms, needing about 300 to 500 ml per gram.
distractor_rationale.D: The camel is quoted as a ureotelic animal that saves a great deal of water, but urea still needs about 50 ml per gram against the far smaller need for uric acid.

solution: Land snails are uricotelic, and uric acid needs only about 5 to 10 ml of water per gram, or none at all. The shark and the camel are ureotelic, needing about 50 ml per gram, and the bony fish is ammonotelic, needing about 300 to 500 ml per gram.
formula_principle: Each group is first assigned its excretory product, then the water cost of that product is applied: uric acid about 5 to 10 ml per gram, urea about 50 ml per gram, ammonia about 300 to 500 ml per gram.

concept_tested: Trading off energy expenditure against water expenditure for two terrestrial animals
stem: Two animals live in the same terrestrial habitat. Animal P eliminates its nitrogenous waste as uric acid and animal Q eliminates it as urea. Which statement about the two is correct?

options.A: P spends less energy in producing its waste and needs less water to eliminate it than Q
options.B: P spends more energy in producing its waste and needs more water to eliminate it than Q
options.C: P spends less energy in producing its waste but needs more water to eliminate it than Q
options.D: P spends more energy in producing its waste but needs less water to eliminate it than Q

correct_answer_text: P spends more energy in producing its waste but needs less water to eliminate it than Q

distractor_rationale.A: Uric acid is the cheaper waste in water but not in energy; uricotelic animals have to spend more energy, not less.
distractor_rationale.B: The energy claim is right but the water claim is not; uric acid needs about 5 to 10 ml per gram against about 50 ml per gram for urea.
distractor_rationale.C: Both halves are inverted, which amounts to treating uricotelism as the cheap and wasteful option instead of the costly and thrifty one.

formula_principle: Water saving in nitrogenous excretion is bought with energy: uricotelic animals spend more energy but need only about 5 to 10 ml of water per gram, while ureotelic animals need about 50 ml per gram.

concept_tested: Recognising that the excretory product may vary within one group of animals
stem: A student states the rule that every animal of a given group excretes the same nitrogenous waste throughout its life. Which pair of observations shows that this rule fails?

options.A: Aquatic invertebrates and bony fishes are both ammonotelic, and mammals and most adult amphibians are both ureotelic
options.B: Birds and many reptiles are both uricotelic, and sharks and rays are both ureotelic
options.C: Spiders and scorpions both excrete guanine, and land snails and some insects both excrete uric acid
options.D: The tadpole of a frog excretes ammonia while adult frogs are mostly ureotelic, and some terrestrial turtles excrete uric acid while others excrete urea or ammonia

correct_answer_text: The tadpole of a frog excretes ammonia while adult frogs are mostly ureotelic, and some terrestrial turtles excrete uric acid while others excrete urea or ammonia

distractor_rationale.A: These pairings show groups agreeing with one another, so they support the student's rule instead of breaking it.
distractor_rationale.B: Here again each pair shares a single mode of excretion, which is exactly what the rule predicts.
distractor_rationale.C: Both pairs are internally consistent, so they illustrate uniformity rather than the variation that would disprove the rule.

formula_principle: There is no clear correlation between phylogenetic relationship and the major excretory product, but habitat does correlate with it, so the product can change with the life stage or between members of one group.

stem: A marine bird and a shark both live in sea water but meet the osmotic challenge differently. Which statement describes the two strategies correctly?

options.B: Both remove excess salts by active transport through glands situated near the nostrils
options.C: Both retain urea in the body fluid so that their body fluid remains isotonic to sea water
options.D: The bird secretes salts by active transport through glands near its nostrils, while the shark retains urea in its body fluid to stay isotonic to sea water

correct_answer_text: The bird secretes salts by active transport through glands near its nostrils, while the shark retains urea in its body fluid to stay isotonic to sea water

formula_principle: Osmoregulation in marine animals takes more than one form: salt glands near the nostrils secrete excess salts by active transport, while retention of urea keeps the body fluid isotonic to sea water.

stem: The human excretory system is made up of a set of organs that produce urine, convey it, store it and finally discharge it to the exterior. Which description gives the correct number of each of these organs?

options.B: One pair of kidneys, one pair of ureters, one urinary bladder and one urethra
options.C: One kidney, one pair of ureters, one urinary bladder and one pair of urethrae
options.D: One pair of kidneys, one pair of ureters, one pair of urinary bladders and one pair of urethrae

options.C: Renal papilla --> minor calyx --> major calyx --> renal pelvis --> ureter

stem: Take the following as the rule: the renal pyramids are the conical arrangement of the medullary structures, and the renal columns, also called the columns of Bertini, are extensions of the cortex lying between the pyramids. A student examining a longitudinal section concludes that every part of the kidney lying deeper than the outer rim must be medullary. Which observation shows this conclusion to be wrong?

options.A: The pyramids themselves are built of cortical tissue and are separated by strips of medulla
options.B: Strips of cortical tissue run inwards between adjacent pyramids as the columns of Bertini
options.C: The renal capsule sends fibrous strips inwards between adjacent pyramids

stem: Take the following as the rule: the two ureters open into the urinary bladder by separate openings, and these openings are NOT guarded by valves. Even so, urine does not flow back into the ureters when a full bladder is compressed. What accounts for this?

options.A: The ureters pass obliquely through the wall of the bladder, so compression closes them
options.B: The two openings lie so far apart on the bladder wall that urine cannot reach them
options.C: A ring of skeletal muscle around each opening contracts as the bladder fills
options.D: The transitional epithelium of the bladder seals each opening as the bladder stretches

correct_answer_text: The ureters pass obliquely through the wall of the bladder, so compression closes them

concept_tested: Attributing the change from alkaline filtrate to acidic urine to the correct step
stem: The glomerular filtrate is alkaline at the time it is formed, yet the urine finally voided is recorded as acidic. Which step of urine formation brings about this change?

options.A: Glomerular filtration into the capsular space of Bowman's capsule
options.B: Selective reabsorption in the proximal convoluted tubule
options.C: Counter current multiplication in the limbs of Henle's loop
options.D: Tubular secretion in the distal convoluted tubule and collecting tubule

correct_answer_text: Tubular secretion in the distal convoluted tubule and collecting tubule

distractor_rationale.A: Filtration produces the alkaline filtrate in the first place, so it cannot be the step that turns the fluid acidic.
distractor_rationale.B: Selective reabsorption returns useful high and low threshold substances to the blood; the change of reaction is not attributed to it.
distractor_rationale.C: The limbs of Henle's loop build the medullary osmotic gradient that concentrates the urine, which is a change in osmolarity and not in reaction.

solution: Tubular secretion, or augmentation, occurring in the distal convoluted tubule and collecting tubule adds H+ and K+ and wastes such as creatinine to the tubular fluid, and this is the step that changes the reaction from alkaline to acidic.
formula_principle: Tubular secretion increases the concentration of the urine and changes its pH from alkaline to acidic by adding H+ and other substances from the blood to the tubular fluid.
common_misconception: Students attribute every change in the character of urine to concentration in Henle's loop, and overlook that the change of reaction is a secretory effect.

stem: A urine report of a healthy person records a specific gravity of 1.02. If the level of antidiuretic hormone in this person rises while everything else remains unchanged, how would the specific gravity of the urine passed behave?

options.A: It would decrease
options.B: It would increase
options.C: It would remain unaffected
options.D: It would first fall and then return to 1.02

correct_answer_text: It would increase

distractor_rationale.A: A fall in specific gravity accompanies diuresis, which follows a decrease and not an increase in antidiuretic hormone.
distractor_rationale.C: Antidiuretic hormone alters the water content of the urine, so a change in its level must be reflected in the specific gravity.

solution: A rise in antidiuretic hormone increases the permeability of the collecting duct wall to water, more water is reabsorbed, the urine becomes more concentrated and its specific gravity rises above the recorded value.
formula_principle: Antidiuretic hormone increases water reabsorption from the collecting ducts, so less water leaves in the urine and the concentration, and therefore the specific gravity, of the urine rises.
common_misconception: Students link antidiuretic hormone to urine volume only and do not carry the reasoning through to the measured concentration of the urine.

concept_tested: Identifying the kidney function that a dialysis machine cannot take over
stem: Dialysis is regarded as a holding measure until a renal transplant can be performed. Which function of the kidney is a dialysis machine unable to take over, and therefore a reason for preferring a transplant?

options.A: Removal of urea and other waste substances from the blood
options.B: Removal of excess salts from the blood
options.C: Secretion of erythropoietin, renin and calcitriol
options.D: Maintenance of the water content of the blood

correct_answer_text: Secretion of erythropoietin, renin and calcitriol

distractor_rationale.A: Waste substances move from the blood into the dialyzing fluid across the membrane, so this function is performed by dialysis.
distractor_rationale.B: Excess salts pass through the membrane into the dialysate, which is isosmotic to normal blood plasma, so dialysis handles this.
distractor_rationale.D: Movement of water and solutes across the dialyzing membrane allows dialysis to act on the water content of the blood.

solution: Dialysis machines can clear wastes and excess salts, but they cannot replace the kidney's secretions of erythropoietin, renin and calcitriol, so dialysis serves only as a holding measure until a renal transplant can be performed.
formula_principle: Dialysis reproduces only the filtering role of the kidney; the endocrine secretions of the kidney are not reproduced by a machine, which is why dialysis is a holding measure until transplant.
common_misconception: Students judge dialysis to be a complete substitute for the kidney because it clears the blood of wastes, forgetting the kidney's secretory functions.
